semantics.xenos_behavior: The predicate is already true at entry in both captured occurrences, so Xenos does not block on either wait.
semantics.native_behavior: Native logs the form unsupported and continues without reading the register or evaluating the predicate. These two instances therefore show an implementation coverage gap, but not a wait-state difference for the observed Xenos register state.

decision.reason: The paired evidence does not show a false register predicate or an ordering difference caused by skipping these waits. Implementing a generic register wait now would require a faithful Native register-state source for false-predicate cases; the current Native ReadRegister path returns zero for most unmodeled registers, so treating that value as authoritative would be an unsupported assumption.
decision.remaining_risk: Other register-form WAIT_REG_MEM commands may have predicates that are false at entry. Native still reports those forms unsupported and does not poll them.
next_evidence_needed: A register-form WAIT_REG_MEM whose predicate is false at Native entry, with Xenos register value captured at the same command.
The preceding register writes or hardware-side state transition that determines that register value, joined to the same PM4 execution order.
A bounded paired rerun showing whether Native must wait for a later external/MMIO or GPU-state update before consuming subsequent packets.

gameplay_limit: Both backends reached Bink 281/281 and original Menu Setup in the documented pair; visible main menu and input consumption remain unconfirmed. This evidence does not explain frontend progression or prove renderer parity.
tests: No code changed. Existing decoder/condition tests were reviewed; no test was added for an unsatisfied register wait because no such captured command/value pair is available.
